findings.description: Scope: SHEET-MARK-002 text only requires anomaly treatment for 'a positive price that rounds to 0 Cents.' The real code guards more broadly — a single `if cents <= 0 { return Err(DegradeReason::SubCent); }` (lib.rs:381-383) degrades ANY non-positive price (exact 0.0 or negative, any magnitude), never emitting Ok(Cents(0)) or a negative Cents. Pinned by test `zero_and_negative_price_are_degraded_not_a_zero_or_negative_mark`: both `price_to_cents(0.0)` and `price_to_cents(-5.0)` assert `Err(SubCent)`. Two of three A-direction sketches (A1, A2), reading the EARS text literally ('a positive price'), implement zero/negative price as an ORDINARY settled/Ok mark and explicitly self-flag this as a spec gap ('may be under-specified,' 'treated as an ordinary zero/negative mark ... the spec text explicitly says a positive price'). All three B-direction reconstructions (B1 item 6, B2 item 6, B3 items 4-5) independently pin the code's broader non-positive guard as behavior the spec text never states. Both directions converge on the same underlying gap.

Non-finite (NaN/±Infinity) price handling is entirely absent from the EARS text. The real code has an explicit two-stage `is_finite()` guard — on the raw `price_usd` (lib.rs:367-369) AND again on the scaled intermediate (lib.rs:374-376) — returning `Err(DegradeReason::Permanent)`, confirmed by `price_to_cents(f64::NAN)` and `price_to_cents(f64::INFINITY)` both asserting `Err(Permanent)`. A1's own hand-rolled implementation would silently produce `Settled(Cents(0))` for NaN input (saturating float→int cast plus `price > 0.0` being false for NaN) — a latent bug A1's own assumption text half-acknowledges ('would misleadingly hit the same price > 0.0 check'); A2 explicitly calls the same gap out ('would produce a garbage cents value ... via as i64'); only A3 independently invented a `NonFinitePrice` anomaly variant. All three B outputs independently pin the Permanent-for-non-finite behavior as code-enforced but spec-silent — same underlying gap surfacing from both directions.

The rounding is not the naive single-step float operation the EARS formula ('round_half_to_even(price × 100)') literally suggests. Code scales through an integer constant `SCALE = 1_000_000` (lib.rs:366): `numerator = (price_usd * 100.0 * SCALE as f64).round() as i128`, then `cents = pt_core::round_half_to_even(numerator, SCALE)` — a two-argument INTEGER helper, not a single-arg f64→i64 rounding function. All three B outputs reconstruct this exact SCALE=1_000_000 mechanism and its stated purpose (decide the half-to-even tie on the integer side, never trusting f64's own rounding). None of this appears in the EARS text, which just states the abstract formula. All three A outputs, lacking this, invented a plain single-step rounding directly on `price*100` (hand-rolled compare-to-0.5 in A1, `f64::round_ties_even` in A2/A3) with a one-argument signature — a structurally different, spec-silent implementation choice from the real two-argument `pt_core::round_half_to_even(numerator, scale)`.

`DegradeReason` collapses two conceptually distinct causes — a genuinely non-positive input price, and a positive price that underflows to exactly 0 cents — into the identical reported reason `SubCent`, via one shared boundary test `cents <= 0` (lib.rs:381). B1 explicitly names this ('a single check ... both classify as SubCent ... the two scenarios are not distinguished by returned reason,' item 8); B3 explicitly notes 'no separate negative price error variant' (item 5). The EARS text's phrasing ('a positive price that rounds to 0 Cents') describes only one scenario; reusing the same reason value for the other (spec-unaddressed) scenario is a code-side representational shortcut the spec never states.

Direction A is internally split 2-1 (A1, A2 vs A3) on whether to invent any handling at all for the two spec-silent edge cases (non-positive price, non-finite price): A1/A2 let both fall through to an ordinary settled mark (self-flagged as gaps); A3 alone invents dedicated anomaly variants for each. This split — not independently grounded in spec text, since the spec is simply silent on both cases — is the generative source of findings 1 and 2 above, and is why A-direction agreement is rated medium rather than high; on its own (absent the code-side confirmation) it would be a mere assumption artifact rather than a finding.

notes: Read both real files directly: crates/sheets-view/src/lib.rs (price_to_cents at lines 362-385, DegradeReason enum at 301-311, read_marks at 817-887) and tests/marks.rs (lines 62-129 cover the conversion + degrade-reason tests). All three B outputs are near-verbatim-accurate reconstructions of the actual SCALE=1_000_000 / two-stage finiteness-guard / cents<=0 collapse — high fidelity to code, and all name behavior (non-finite→Permanent, non-positive→SubCent, SCALE constant) with zero basis in the literal EARS text, which only mentions the positive-rounds-to-zero case. Direction A's core unanimous behavior (price>0 && cents==0 → anomaly) exactly matches spec text and IS satisfied by the real code, so that portion is BD-COHERENT; the drift lives specifically in the two edge cases spec is silent on (non-positive input, non-finite input) where code enforces guards beyond the letter of SHEET-MARK-002, and where 2 of 3 A-sketches, taking the spec at its word, would have shipped materially different (arguably wrong/buggy) behavior for those same inputs. That two-sided convergence is what drives the BD-DRIFT call rather than a plain B-ONLY-DRIFT.
